model_configuration:
Findings. (measured) marks what the evidence shows; (inferred) marks my reading.

(1) Did the deep configuration find operationally significant defects that a standard configuration would likely have missed? Mostly no (inferred). The significant finds of the day were deterministic executability defects found by running or simulating things:
- The AF preflight simulated the plan and found 48 of 172 fixture cases failing and 18 error codes (measured, AF record :745-747).
- R3-01 was a code-order bug: land.py's check returned before fill(). Any rehearsal of the CL-40 readback exposes it. The pass-4 land.py rehearsal did exactly that once someone thought to run it (measured, record :754-755).
- R4-06 was missed by the full, deep rounds 2 and 3. It was found in round 4 by a reviewer who fetched the live AF list, a read-only dry run of a control-page readback (measured, process-review critiques[1].corrections[9]). Pass 6 later ran such helpers on the live pages (record :773-774).
- R5-07 (the D24 brief left unwritten) and R6-09 (no readback tool) are 'the verification names no committed tool' defects. A mechanical check that every step's inputs and commands exist finds them without depth (inferred).
- So a cheap dry run of every normal-path gate on the landed text, plus that existence check, would likely have found R3-01, R4-06, R5-07 and R6-09 by about round 2 (inferred; the RCA's change 1 cost column agrees).
- The deep rounds did find real, subtle silent-outcome defects (R5-03, R6-02, R6-08). All of them were in machinery the deep loop itself had added (measured, defects-by-round.csv originB 'ii').
- The one breadth win is the ANALYZE body sweep: 184 REAL findings across 55 bodies, which the AF close-out had missed. It came from fan-out and refute-by-default judging, not from depth. A standard configuration with an explicit old-text search (RCA change 11) would likely have found most of it (inferred).

(2) Did it mainly widen the review surface? Yes (measured):
- 3 lenses plus 3 verifiers per round, 14 workflows and 87 subagents.
- Every round re-read up to 425 KB, and 25-33% of reports were duplicates.
- Failure and resume terms in the lens prompts went from 0 to 59.
- execution-and-delegation-model.md §1 carries the session's setting to every subagent, so cost scaled with the fan-out.

(3) Did it encourage broad rewrites? It contributed (inferred causal link, measured growth):
- The spec went from 190,729 to 425,130 B, and the machinery sections about ×6, while §3 grew 2.7%.
- Decisions went from 56 to 119, plan Python from 2,408 to 6,415 lines, and registry assertions from 1,484 to 2,024.
- The mode's 'token cost is not a constraint' removed the budget signal: the 1-2M estimate was passed by 22:43 and never re-priced.
- It was not the cause of the loop. Under the same mode, ANALYZE (entered 17:57:41, exited 20:33:16) converged in 3 rounds. The difference was review design ('Try hard' in PLAN prompts only, no refute-by-default in PLAN, a self-set zero exit) and Nathan's absence.
- The mode's own patterns (dedupe against a fixed target, refute-by-default majority) were not followed (process-review critiques[0].corrections[13]).
- Limit: the evidence cannot separate the effect of the reasoning-effort level from that of the Ultracode multi-agent mode. Who re-enabled it at 21:07:41 is not verified, though the evidence points to Nathan's side.

(4) Should it be the default for routine maintenance? No. Use a standard configuration, with a mandatory mechanical dry run of normal-path gates and a single consolidated gate, as in ecosystem-change-management.md §7 and execution-and-delegation-model §0A. Escalate only on the triggers in escalation_triggers, and drop back to standard once the dry run passes on the normal path. Here that point was pass 4 at 02:06Z, with 51 of 51 bodies passing.
escalation_triggers:
Escalate to a deep, multi-agent review only on evidence, and scope it to the triggering surface. Triggers:
- (a) A completion claim has been refuted, or a check was shown to test only the new wording. Example: 18:37, where the D23 'complete' claim failed. Response: a corpus-wide breadth sweep with refute-by-default verifiers, as in the ANALYZE body sweep, once.
- (b) A cheap dry run or preflight returns WOULD_FAIL on the normal path. Example: the AF preflight's 48 of 172 fixture failures. Response: a deeper check of that plan's executability, then a return to Nathan.
- (c) The change can silently breach a Product Owner ruling (D22, D24, no subagent for PR-35) or silently mis-edit a live body or control page. Response: deep review of that path only.
- (d) The change creates or re-pins an oracle, a validator or a guard whose failure is silent. Examples: the R1 successor, FMV guards.
- (e) The blast radius is Tier 1 or above across many release members, for example more than about 10 live bodies or more than one skill package (inferred threshold).

Do not escalate because a review round found more defects in machinery a repair just added. That is the non-convergence signal, and the right response is to return to Nathan, not to review more deeply. De-escalate once the normal-path dry run passes and the distinct confirmed required defects stop halving.
stopping_rule_candidates:
RULE 1: review cap with a dry-run floor. Where: modification-template.md as a new rule 8, and the PLAN-review brief.
- The rule: before the first full review, run a mechanical dry run of every normal-path gate and readback on the landed text (read-only against live pages), and check that every step's verification names a committed command. Then allow at most two full reviews (the first, and one after its repair), then one check scoped to the repair diff.
- Then the plan goes to Nathan with every open finding listed by path, likelihood and consequence, whatever the count. A round in which both reviewers confirm, or which has zero REQUIRED findings, ends reviewing. Its non-blocking findings go to the Backlog or are listed as accepted risks, and repairing them is opt-in and priced.
- Evidence it would have stopped well: pass 4 (02:06Z) and the live-page helpers were available, and they cover R3-01, R4-06, R5-07 and R6-09 (inferred). The plan would have reached Nathan after R2, its repair and a diff check, around 01:45-02:15Z. By 08:25 it would have been waiting with its risks listed, instead of absent.
- In the AF skill review it stops at a3 (FIT/FIT), avoiding a4 and a5 and the regression the hardening introduced (SFR-A4-2 F1).
- In closeout ANALYZE it matches what happened: stop at round 3.
- Risk: defects in unchanged text that the dry run does not exercise can ship unlisted (R4-07 async polling, R3-07 continuity, R5-03). The first plan's single-sentence failure design would still need fixing within the two rounds.

RULE 2: non-convergence or regression trigger. Where: session-working-rules.md, and a PLAN-review brief field.
- The rule: after each round, count distinct confirmed REQUIRED defects in one unit. If the count does not at least halve from the previous round, or if more than half sit in text the last repair added, stop and send a DECISION NEEDED. It carries the trend, the open findings with path and likelihood, and three options: approve with listed risks, one more diff check, or simplify.
- Evidence: PLAN R2 had 8, R3 had 9 (7 in repair-added text), so it fires at about 01:47Z. ANALYZE round 2 had 14, all against the repair, so it fires at about 20:00 while Nathan was present; he was then asked rulings anyway, so the cost is small. In the AF skill review, a1 had 1 required defect and a2 had 2, so it fires after a2, and Nathan was already approving each repair set.
- Risk: small counts are noisy, so it can fire early on a converging loop (1 to 2). Each firing costs Nathan one message, and it depends on counting honestly: the RCA found mixed report and defect units in the session's own series.

RULE 3: exit-rule provenance and budget re-price. Where: session-working-rules.md and glow-po-reporting.
- The rule: the session may not tighten an exit rule Nathan approved without asking him. Any stopping rule it states is labelled with who set it and when, and a compaction summary quotes the commitment and Nathan's reply verbatim. When elapsed time or tokens pass twice the estimate Nathan approved, the session stops and re-prices with a DECISION NEEDED before its next round.
- Evidence: the approved estimate was 1-2M tokens and about 1 h. Drafting alone passed 4M tokens by 22:43, so the rule fires before R2. The 00:32 gate change ('once that review is clean') was a tightening of the 23:58 commitment Nathan had answered at 00:13, and it would have required asking him. In the AF run, interaction cost went from 11 predicted to 29 actual, so a round-trip budget would have fired at the a3 hardening decision, pricing it at two or more rounds before Nathan chose.
- Risk: estimates are rough, so this can interrupt a healthy run, and the cost is one message. Enforcement depends on the session, because nothing in the repository can see a transcript. The only guard is the report itself.
